text:
Winnipeg arrives in Raleigh winless in eight (0-6-2), coming off a 5-2 loss at Florida in which Anton Lundell scored three. The Jets have been outscored 30-16 during the skid, and the chances back that up: they've had 44% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality. They're also without Josh Morrissey, with Neal Pionk now logging 24:27 a night. Carolina has won three straight and is 4-0-1 in its last five, even without Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal. Nikolaj Ehlers has moved onto Hall's wing, and Mark Jankowski is playing more. Carolina won the Oct. 17 meeting 3-2.

The numbers favor Carolina. At five on five, the Hurricanes have 59% of the expected goals against 45% for Winnipeg, and our model projects 3.63 goals for CAR against 2.54 for WPG. On special teams, Carolina's power play (0.89 expected goals a game) faces a Jets penalty kill allowing 0.84, and the Hurricanes take over four penalties a game. In net, projected starters Stuart Skinner and Pyotr Kochetkov are both positive in goals saved above expected (+4.1 and +6.7), though Skinner carried a heavier load last season.

For Winnipeg, Kyle Connor has a 38% chance to score and Mark Scheifele 29%. Jackson Blake is on a five-game point streak, and as Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal posted, Ehlers has a "team-leading ninth of the year." Our under-the-radar pick is Jankowski: his 3.4 expected goals over 10 games rate better than 98% of depth forwards, and we have him at 24% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
